name: Stylianos Syropoulos
bio: Stylianos (Stelios) Syropoulos is the Director of of the Intergenerational Decisions and Effective Action (IDEA) Lab. His work seeks to understand the human dimensions of sustainability, by studying individual differences and interventions to promote sustainable living. Broader interests include human morality, prosociality, intergenerational decisions and intergroup conflict. Prior to starting the IDEA lab, he was a postdoctoral researcher in the Morality Lab, the Social Influence and Social Change Lab, and the The Schiller Institute for Integrated Science and Society at Boston College. He obtained his Ph.D. in social psychology from the University of Massachusetts Amherst.

name: Christina Jinhee (Jin) Capozzoli
bio: Christina Jinhee (Jin) Capozzoli is a first year PhD student in the IDEA lab. She is interested in how the psychology of morality, affect, and prosocial behavior can be applied to solve pressing societal problems, such as sustainability. Previously, she has worked in social neuroscience and psychology labs at Columbia University and at NYU, before beginning a Master of Applied Statistics at Penn State. Her past research projects have spanned from developmental neuroscience to moral expansiveness to climate change risk perception.

name: Sarah Gonzalez-Coffin
bio: Sarah Gonzalez-Coffin, PhD, is an interdisciplinary social scientist who studies how people make decisions about solutions to complex social and environmental challenges. Trained as a social psychologist in the Environment, Decision, Judgment, and Identity lab at the University of Colorado Boulder (PI: Dr. Leaf Van Boven), Sarah’s research focuses on decision making, drivers of policy support, climate change communication, and public adoption/opposition of renewable energy, carbon dioxide removal, alternative proteins, and transmission infrastructure technologies. She has co-authored reports for the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. Grid Deployment Office, worked with the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and North Central Climate Adaptation Science Center, and received the 2023 Emerging Scholar Award from the Association for Psychological Science.

name: Jade Wing
bio: Jade Wing is a current Arizona State University student actively pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Psychology (B.S.) and a minor in Sustainability. In the near future, he intends to pursue a PhD in Psychology. His goal throughout his academic and professional career is to participate in research that will aid global sustainable efforts and humanitarian aid. His other interests are in photo journalism; he hopes to use his experiences to bridge social gaps and engage with people currently in crisis.

name: Magdalyn (Maggie) Smith
bio: Maggie Rath is an Undergraduate Research Assistant in the IDEA Lab at Arizona State University. She is majoring in Psychology with a minor in Philosophy. Her research interests are in the psychology of religion. Currently she is working on a project focusing on public perceptions of religious leaders in the US. After completing her B.S., Maggie plans to pursue a Ph.D. in Psychology. She hopes to become a professor studying the psychology of religion in families, communities, and individuals.

name: Duncan Ward
bio: Dunca Ward received bachelor's degrees in Psychology and Economics from Grinnell College where he completed independent research examining the collective action of climate change from both psychological and political economic perspectives. Since graduating, Duncan has focused on individuals' behaviors and motivations as they pertain to energy efficiency and electrification. Currently, Duncan is a Senior Quantitative Analyst at Apex Analytics where his work ranges from evaluation support for the Inflation Reduction Act's HEAR and HOMES programs to statistical analyses of heat pump user's cold weather heating behaviors.

name: Wakana Matsumoto
bio: Wakana Matsumoto earned bachelor’s degrees in Psychology and Sociology from UCLA, where she completed a departmental honors thesis examining the effects of moral education interventions on sustainable decision-making. She is currently pursuing her master’s degree at the Humboldt University of Berlin’s School of Mind and Brain, where she investigates decision-making mechanisms in social contexts—particularly how cultural, social, and situational factors shape individual perception and behavior. Wakana aspires to contribute to resolving social issues through psychological approaches, which motivates her to uncover scientific interventions to promote prosocial behaviors across the broader population.

name: Elda Bengu
bio: Elda Bengu earned her bachelor’s degree in Psychology from Arizona State University in 2025. Currently, she is working towards her Master’s in Psychology of Global Mobility, Inclusion and Diversity at the University of Oslo in Norway. Her master’s research will examine climate- induced resource scarcity and its implications for intergroup cooperation. In the future, she intends to pursue a PhD in Social Psychology, with the aim of applying social psychological perspectives to pressing real-world challenges.

name: Marisa Granados
bio: Marisa Granados earned her bachelor’s degree in Ecosystem Science and Sustainability from Colorado State University in 2022. There, she participated in extensive ecological research and developed an original survey tool to measure students’ confidence in course competencies and learning objectives. She stepped away from academia to clarify her interests and returned with a passion for solving environmental problems while utilizing social and developmental psychology perspectives. Currently, she is a volunteer research assistant in John Coley’s CORE lab at Northeastern and is continuing her post-baccalaureate studies in Psychology and data analysis. She hopes to research qualities of early social and learning contexts and their effect on lasting belief in collective action.

name: Grace Bauer
bio: Grace Bauer is a current senior at Boston College pursuing a B.S. in Neuroscience and a B.A. in Philosophy. Her research interests are primarily in predictive processing and how representations of objects, scenes, and memories contribute to our understanding of reality. She is currently working on her senior thesis in object representations, investigating the role that object states play in object similarity. In the future, she plans to pursue a PhD in Cognitive Science to study how humans construct reality in naturalistic settings.

name: Mochi Wu
bio: Mochi is a 7-year old calico female kitty who has been with Stelios and his research partner and wife Dr. Deborah Wu (fellow Assistant Professor at ASU) for 4 years now. During her tenure, she has definitely grown, well at least physically, as she gained 2 pounds. The vet says she is a happy kitty who is enjoying herself, so she is fine. In fact she is no more than 11 pounds! Her research interests include finding treats, playing with her toys, and meowing excessively whenever she is hungry (which feels like it's all the time). Mochi's goal is to maintain her fluffiness at all costs, so she sleeps at least 12-15 hours a day, but when she is awake, she wants your attention.

name: Kyle Fiore Law
bio: Kyle is a social psychologist working at the intersection of moral psychology and ethical philosophy trying to better understand the outer limits of human cooperation and prosocial behavior. In particular, his research focuses on mapping the cognitive, affective, and moral architecture of exceptional altruism, driven by an underlying motivation to harness insights gleaned from the laboratory to help inspire real-world action. Prior to joining the IDEA Lab, Kyle worked as a postdoctoral researcher in The Morality Lab at Boston College under the mentorship of Dr. Liane Young. Before that, he earned his PhD in the Imagination and Cognition Lab at SUNY Albany under the supervision of Dr. Brendan Bo O'Connor.
now: Since his departure from the IDEA lab, Kyle started an Assistant Professor position at the University of Utah where he directs the Morality, Altruism, and Prosociality Lab

name: Eliza J. DelaPaz
bio: Eliza DelaPaz is a Marine Corps veteran and Neuroscience major at Arizona State University. She recently completed the Warrior Scholar Project at Yale and currently serves as a Research Assistant with the Veterans Imagination Project at the Center for Science and the Imagination. Her research explores adversity, resilience, and human flourishing through neuroscience, mindfulness, and storytelling. Eliza previously led entrepreneurial ventures in West Africa and later undertook a transformative sabbatical across the continent, including time in Zanzibar and Egypt’s Red Sea region—experiences that deepened her commitment to healing and service. She now serves as Child Sponsorship Manager for the nonprofit Songea’s Kids and teaches yoga to veterans to support mental well-being.
now: Since her departure from the IDEA lab, Eliza has continued her work as a certified life coach and also started working as a child sponsorship manager at Songea's Kids.

name: Zhaoquan Wang
bio: Zhaoquan (Harold) Wang received dual degrees in Psychology (B.S.) and Economics (B.A.) with honors from Boston College. Prior to joining the IDEA Lab, he completed two honors theses under the supervision of Dr. Liane Young in the Morality Lab and served as a summer research assistant under Dr. Laura Niemi and Dr. John Doris in the Cornell Applied Moral Psychology Lab. His broader research interests include moral judgment, social perception, justice, and punishment. After graduation, he plans to pursue graduate studies to further explore the cognitive mechanisms underlying contemporary social issues and moral dilemmas.
now: Since his departure from the IDEA lab, Zhaoquan joined the Social Psychology PhD program at University of California Santa Barbara working with Dr. Heejung Kim.

name: Kearney Capuano
bio: Kearney graduated from Georgetown University with a B.S. in Global Health, Psychology, and Philosophy. She currently works at Open Philanthropy supporting the Effective Giving and Business Operations Teams. At Georgetown, she researched under Abigail Marsh in the Laboratory on Social and Affective Neuroscience, in addition to being selected as a research fellow in Georgetown’s inaugural Global Health Institute. She also served as a summer research assistant at Yale University’s Affect Regulation and Cognition lab. Prior to joining Open Philanthropy, Kearney founded her university Effective Altruism Organization, interned at Giving What We Can and The Global Challenges Project, and worked as a Global Health Associate at Chemonics International. Her broader research interests include moral decision making, prosociality, and the psychological underpinnings of effective altruism.
now: Kearney has been working as a Program Associate in the Effective Giving & Careers track at Coefficient Giving.
